acceptance_criteria.criterion: The api object in api.js exposes all endpoint methods: repositories (5 methods: list, get, create, update, delete), projects (8 methods: list, get, create, update, rename, delete, addRepository, removeRepository), workspaces (6 methods: list, get, create, update, rename, delete), branches (2 methods: list, switch), and status (2 methods: get, refresh).

API methods construct correct URLs matching the backend routes (e.g., api.workspaces.list('proj1') calls GET /api/projects/proj1/workspaces, api.projects.rename('p1', 'p2') calls PUT /api/projects/p1/rename with body {newId: 'p2'}).
Non-2xx API responses result in a thrown Error containing the server's error message parsed from the JSON response body.
showConfirm(title, message) renders a modal overlay with title, message, Cancel and Confirm buttons, and returns a Promise that resolves on confirm and rejects on cancel.
createStatusBadge(gitStatusInfo) returns a DOM element displaying branch name, modified file count, commits ahead/behind, last activity, and conflict indicator with appropriate CSS classes.
showToast(message, type) appends a notification element to #toast-container with the given type class (success, error, info) that auto-dismisses after a timeout.
createFormField() and validateRequired() are exported from form-helpers.js and generate labeled form inputs and inline validation error display respectively.

summary: Created gui/public/js/api.js: exports `api` object with all 5 namespaces (repositories×5, projects×8, workspaces×6, branches×2, status×2). Internal `request()` helper handles fetch, JSON parsing, 204 No Content, and non-2xx error extraction from `error` field in JSON body.

Created gui/public/js/components/confirm-dialog.js: exports `showConfirm(title, message)`. Renders modal overlay using .modal-overlay/.modal CSS classes. Returns a Promise — resolves on Confirm, rejects on Cancel or Escape key. Backdrop click also cancels. Cleans up DOM and keyboard listener on close.

Created gui/public/js/components/status-badge.js: exports `createStatusBadge(gitStatusInfo)`. Handles null with 'No data' element. Priority-ordered CSS class selection (conflict > modified > ahead > behind > clean). Detail row shows modified count, commits ahead/behind, relative last-activity timestamp, and conflict warning.

Created gui/public/js/components/toast.js: exports `showToast(message, type, duration?)`. Appends to #toast-container. Classes: toast toast-{type}. Auto-dismisses after 4 s with CSS slide-out animation. Includes manual close button. Guard against double-dismiss.

Created gui/public/js/components/form-helpers.js: exports `createFormField(label, type, name, opts)` supporting input/select/textarea types, and `validateRequired(form, fields)` with per-field inline `.field-error` spans, CSS `error` class on controls, and focus management for accessibility.
All 5 files verified: ESM syntax clean, all named exports resolve to functions.

comments.note: api.js uses encodeURIComponent on all URL segments — correct and defensive. Worth noting for future maintainers: if the backend ever starts accepting slash-containing IDs, this encoding would need review.
toast.js: the close button uses inline style for margin/font-size rather than a dedicated CSS class. A small `.toast-close` rule in styles.css would be cleaner and easier to theme.

confirm-dialog.js: focus is moved to the Confirm button on open for accessibility; however, there is no focus-trap implemented (Tab can escape the modal). A full trap is low-priority for an internal tool but worth adding if keyboard-only users are a concern.

status-badge.js uses `status-badge-ahead` / `status-badge-behind` CSS classes for the primary pill; the spec mentions `status-clean`, `status-modified`, `status-ahead-behind`, `status-conflict`. The styles.css uses `status-badge-*` names consistently — implementation follows the stylesheet rather than the spec prose.

form-helpers.js uses CSS.escape() to safely interpolate field names into querySelector attribute selectors — good defensive practice. This API is widely supported but technically still prefixed in some older environments; if IE/old-Edge support is ever required it would need a polyfill.

summary: Verified all 5 new files (api.js, confirm-dialog.js, status-badge.js, toast.js, form-helpers.js) against all 7 Acceptance Criteria using a custom 73-test jsdom/Node.js test suite. 73/73 tests passed.

AC2 PASS — URL construction verified for 10 representative route patterns including encodeURIComponent encoding, correct request bodies (newId, assignments, repositoryId), and correct HTTP methods. Tests were run sequentially to avoid shared-fetch-mock races.
AC3 PASS — Non-2xx responses throw Error with server's 'error' JSON field; falls back to statusText when body is non-JSON; 204 resolves to undefined.

AC4 PASS — showConfirm: modal overlay present with title/message/buttons; Promise resolves on Confirm click; rejects on Cancel click, Escape key, and backdrop click; DOM cleanup confirmed in all paths.

AC5 PASS — createStatusBadge: returns 'No data' element for null input; shows branch name, detached HEAD, modified count, ahead/behind counts, last activity, conflict chip; CSS class priority (conflict > modified > ahead > behind > clean) verified.

AC6 PASS — showToast: appends to #toast-container with correct class (toast-success/error/info); returns element; stacking verified (5 simultaneous toasts); close button triggers removing class; double-dismiss guard works; returns null when container absent.

AC7 PASS — createFormField: generates form-group div, label, input/select/textarea, required asterisk, pre-populated value, hint text, hidden .field-error span. validateRequired: returns true/false correctly; clears all listed-field errors before re-validation; shows inline error with 'error' CSS class; handles unknown field names gracefully. comments.note: form-helpers.js uses CSS.escape() in validateRequired() to safely interpolate field names into querySelector selectors. CSS.escape() is not available in jsdom (test environments) and is also absent in IE11/old-Edge. While these environments are unlikely targets for this tool, a small inline fallback (e.g. value.replace(/([^\w-])/g, '\\$1')) would make the function portable across all runtimes without adding a dependency.
confirm-dialog.js does not implement a focus trap — Tab can escape the modal. For an internal tool this is low priority but worth tracking if keyboard-only accessibility is required in future.
toast.js close button uses inline style properties (marginLeft, fontSize, lineHeight) rather than a CSS class. A .toast-close rule in styles.css would be cleaner and easier to theme or override.

api.js always sends Content-Type: application/json even for GET/DELETE requests with no body. While harmless, stripping it for bodyless requests is conventional and avoids confusing some strict servers.

toast.js and status-badge.js were tested with 5-toast stacking and conflict-priority CSS class ordering respectively — both behave correctly. The auto-dismiss timer (4 s) was not unit-tested (requires fake timers) but the guard against double-dismiss was verified independently.

summary: Reviewed 5 files: gui/public/js/api.js, confirm-dialog.js, status-badge.js, toast.js, form-helpers.js. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 0 Medium findings. 2 Low findings noted (CSS class injection in showToast; server error message propagation). All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A03 / A04 (Injection / Insecure Design) — toast.js line 89: showToast() interpolates the caller-supplied `type` parameter directly into a CSS className string: `toast.className = `toast toast-${type}``. No sanitization or allowlist check is applied. In current usage the caller always passes a literal string ('success', 'error', 'info', 'warning'), so there is no real exploit path. However, if a future caller passes attacker-influenced data, an unexpected CSS class name could be injected. Remediation (defence-in-depth): add an allowlist guard — e.g., `const VALID_TYPES = new Set(['success','error','info','warning']); const safeType = VALID_TYPES.has(type) ? type : 'info';` — before constructing the className. This closes the theoretical CSS class injection vector entirely.

A09 (Security Logging) / A05 — api.js lines 61-63: The server-supplied `error` field from the JSON response body is propagated verbatim into the thrown Error message. For an internal, locally-run developer tool with a single authenticated user this is appropriate and intentional. Note for future maintainers: if this API client is ever used in a multi-user or network-exposed context, server error messages should be treated as untrusted input and filtered before display to avoid information leakage from verbose backend errors.

A03 (Injection) — form-helpers.js lines 219/231: validateRequired() uses CSS.escape() to safely escape field names before interpolating them into a querySelector attribute selector (`[name="${CSS.escape(fieldName)}"]`). This is good defensive practice that correctly prevents selector injection. Note already raised by Dev/QA: CSS.escape() is a browser-only API absent in jsdom and IE11; an inline polyfill (e.g., fieldName.replace(/([^\w-])/g, '\\$1')) would make the function runtime-portable without adding any dependency.

Positive finding — all 5 files use `.textContent` exclusively for DOM text insertion (never .innerHTML or .outerHTML), consistently preventing DOM-based XSS. All URL path segments in api.js are wrapped in encodeURIComponent(). confirm-dialog.js and status-badge.js insert all dynamic data via textContent or createTextNode(). No injection surface was identified.

summary: Reviewed 5 files: gui/public/js/api.js, gui/public/js/components/confirm-dialog.js, status-badge.js, toast.js, form-helpers.js. All 7 acceptance criteria confirmed met. Code quality is high: clean ESM module structure, excellent JSDoc coverage, strong defensive practices (textContent-only DOM insertion, encodeURIComponent on all URL segments, CSS.escape() in selectors), and consistent naming conventions throughout.

api.js — Architecture is well-factored: single internal request() helper with clean separation of concerns. The 204 handling (return undefined), the Content-Type-gated JSON parse, and the error field extraction all reflect mature HTTP client design. Minor: Content-Type: application/json is always sent even on GET/DELETE (harmless but non-conventional). The export shape (named api object with namespace sub-objects) is clean and extensible.

confirm-dialog.js — Promise-based modal idiom is correct. All three cancellation paths (Cancel button, Escape key, backdrop click) correctly call the same onCancel() handler and converge through the same cleanup() function, preventing any double-resolve/reject race. Accessibility attributes (role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby) are present and correct. Only gap: no focus trap on Tab — acceptable for an internal tool but documented.

status-badge.js — resolveBadgeClass() correctly encodes the priority order (conflict > modified > ahead > behind > clean). formatLastActivity() is a clean, self-contained relative-time formatter with sensible fallback for unparseable timestamps. The conditional detail-row rendering (only append if has children) avoids emitting empty DOM nodes. The 'detached HEAD' fallback for null currentBranch is the correct git term.

toast.js — The double-dismiss guard (dataset.dismissing flag) is a well-chosen approach that prevents clearTimeout + DOM-removal races. TOAST_DISPLAY_MS / TOAST_ANIMATION_MS named constants make the timing relationship with CSS immediately clear. The getContainer() lazy-get + console.warn on missing container is good defensive UX. Minor: close button uses inline styles (marginLeft, fontSize, lineHeight) rather than a .toast-close CSS class — flagged by Dev/QA/Security and confirmed low-priority.

form-helpers.js — Two-pass validate-then-report pattern (clear all errors first, then re-validate) avoids stale error state correctly. The random suffix on fieldId (field-${name}-${random}) prevents ID collisions when the same name is reused in multiple forms. Error clearing on 'input' events gives immediate feedback. CSS.escape() usage in validateRequired() is sound security practice; the browser-only caveat has been noted by Dev, QA, and Security Auditor — no action required for this tool's target environment.
Security findings from prior audit are all low-priority and non-blocking: (1) toast type allowlist hardening, (2) CSS.escape() portability. Both are tracked. No blocking findings.
Code-review verdict: PASS. Code is production-ready for an internal developer tool. Three low-priority non-blocking recommendations forwarded to Documentation.

comments.note: api.js request(): Content-Type: application/json is sent unconditionally for all HTTP methods, including GET and DELETE (which have no body). While most servers ignore extraneous headers, this is non-conventional and could confuse strict proxies or CORS preflight logic. Recommended fix: only set Content-Type when body !== undefined (i.e., inside the existing `if (body !== undefined)` block). The Accept: application/json header is always appropriate and can remain unconditional.

api.js request(): When the response Content-Type is not application/json (e.g., plain text error from a proxy), the json variable stays undefined and the error path falls back to response.statusText. This is correct behaviour but could be slightly more informative: if the response body is plain text and the server is not JSON-capable, statusText (e.g., 'Bad Gateway') is less actionable than the actual body text. A future enhancement: attempt response.text() as a secondary fallback for non-JSON error bodies.

confirm-dialog.js: The aria-labelledby and aria-describedby attributes use hard-coded IDs ('confirm-dialog-title', 'confirm-dialog-body'). If showConfirm() is ever called while a prior dialog is still open (concurrent calls), both dialogs will emit duplicate IDs in the DOM, which is invalid HTML and breaks screen-reader label association. For this tool's single-user synchronous usage this is not a real issue, but generating unique IDs (e.g., using crypto.randomUUID() or a simple counter) would be a robust improvement.

status-badge.js: The spec (WP-002.md) mentions CSS classes `status-clean`, `status-modified`, `status-ahead-behind`, `status-conflict` for color-coding. The implementation correctly follows the actual stylesheet's `status-badge-clean`, `status-badge-modified`, `status-badge-ahead`, `status-badge-behind`, `status-badge-conflict` conventions instead. This is the right call — implementation follows the authoritative source (styles.css) over the spec prose. The spec should be updated to reflect the actual class names to avoid future confusion.

toast.js: The close button styles (marginLeft: 'auto', fontSize: '1.1rem', lineHeight: '1', pointerEvents: 'auto') are applied via inline JS style properties. The button already has className 'btn-icon toast-close', so these rules belong in styles.css under .toast-close { margin-left: auto; font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1; }. This was noted by Dev, QA, and Security Auditor — confirmed low-priority, but a concrete CSS rule would be cleaner and enable theming.

toast.js: showToast() accepts a `type` parameter typed as 'success'|'error'|'info'|'warning' in JSDoc but performs no runtime validation before interpolating it into className. As flagged by the Security Auditor: adding a Set-based allowlist guard (`const VALID_TYPES = new Set(['success','error','info','warning']); const safeType = VALID_TYPES.has(type) ? type : 'info';`) is a one-liner defence-in-depth improvement. Non-blocking for this internal tool but recommended before any future widening of the call surface.

form-helpers.js validateRequired(): CSS.escape() is correct and safe in browser environments. As noted by Dev, QA, and Security Auditor, it is absent in jsdom and IE11. The recommended inline fallback — `const esc = typeof CSS !== 'undefined' && CSS.escape ? CSS.escape : (s) => s.replace(/([^\w-])/g, '\\$1');` — adds zero dependencies and makes the function portable across all JS runtimes. Non-blocking for production browser usage.

form-helpers.js createFormField(): the auto-generated fieldId uses Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,7) — a 5-character base-36 random suffix giving ~60 million combinations. This is sufficient to prevent collisions in practice, but crypto.randomUUID() or a monotonic counter (let _id = 0; const fieldId = overrideId || `field-${name}-${++_id}`) would be both collision-free and deterministic (useful for snapshot tests and SSR). Medium priority because the current approach is functionally correct but the collision risk, while tiny, is non-zero.

confirm-dialog.js: No focus trap is implemented — pressing Tab while the modal is open allows focus to reach underlying page controls. For an internal developer tool this is acceptable. If accessibility compliance (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.2) is ever required, a full focus-trap implementation (intercept Tab/Shift+Tab and cycle within the modal) should be added. This has been consistently noted by Dev, QA, and Security Auditor.
